blocks.label: Career category

QUALIFICATION
Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies
Economics & Finance (Liberal)
CAREER LEVEL
Entry-level
Research Assistant / Junior Economic Researcher, depending on employer requirements

An Economic Researcher studies how individuals, businesses, markets, and governments make decisions about resources. Economic researchers analyse economic trends, financial conditions, public policies, employment, inflation, trade, inequality, and business activity to develop evidence-based insights.

A degree in Economics & Finance provides a foundation in economic theory, financial systems, markets, and quantitative analysis. A liberal studies approach can also strengthen communication, critical thinking, and understanding of social and institutional factors influencing economic outcomes.
Economic researchers may work in banks, financial institutions, consulting firms, think tanks, universities, government agencies, and international development organisations.

Career progression
Progression depends on the employer and the complexity of the work. Some economist and advanced research positions require a master's degree or PhD.
Year 1
Foundation
Understand economic systems

items.text: Learn introductory microeconomics and macroeconomics.
Understand supply and demand, market structures, inflation, unemployment, and economic growth.
Build foundational mathematics, probability, and statistics.
Learn spreadsheet skills using Excel or Google Sheets.
Follow reports from India's Ministry of Finance, the Reserve Bank of India, and other credible economic sources.
Practise writing short explanations of economic developments.

blocks.text: Year 2
Methods
Develop analytical and research skills

items.text: Study intermediate microeconomics and macroeconomics.
Learn statistical inference, regression, and introductory econometrics.
Understand financial markets, monetary policy, fiscal policy, and international trade.
Learn how to clean, organise, and visualise economic datasets.
Start using R, Python, or Stata for statistical analysis.
Write a research brief using publicly available economic data.

blocks.text: Year 3
Application
Build an economic research portfolio

items.text: Study applied econometrics, research design, and causal inference fundamentals.
Select a specialisation such as macroeconomics, public finance, labour economics, or financial economics.
Analyse inflation, employment, household spending, trade, or industry-level data.
Complete a research paper with transparent methods and limitations.
Apply for internships with research institutions, banks, think tanks, and consulting firms.
Present findings through charts, concise reports, and presentations.

blocks.text: Year 4
If applicable
Prepare for research roles or postgraduate study

items.text: Complete an honours thesis or advanced research project.
Learn more advanced econometric techniques and data reproducibility.
Develop a writing sample and research portfolio.
Practise interpreting research findings and explaining their policy or business implications.
Apply for research analyst and assistant economist roles.
Consider postgraduate economics training for roles requiring deeper quantitative expertise.

blocks.text: Adapt this plan to the programme's duration and curriculum. A three-year degree can cover the same core competencies on a compressed timeline.
A. Macroeconomic Research
Studies national and global economic performance, inflation, growth, interest rates, employment, and monetary policy.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Macroeconomics, time-series analysis, econometrics, economic forecasting.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Macroeconomic Research Analyst, Economic Research Assistant.
B. Public Policy Research
Evaluates taxes, government expenditure, welfare programmes, labour markets, and public-sector interventions.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Policy evaluation, applied statistics, research writing, programme assessment.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Policy Research Analyst, Public Finance Research Assistant.
C. Financial and Banking Research
Studies financial markets, credit conditions, banking trends, asset markets, and the relationship between finance and the economy.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Financial economics, quantitative analysis, financial statements, market research.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Financial Research Analyst, Banking Research Analyst, Economic Analyst.
D. Labour and Development Economics
Examines employment, wages, education, poverty, inequality, productivity, and economic development.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Survey data analysis, econometrics, impact evaluation, field research.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Development Research Analyst, Labour Economics Research Assistant.
E. Industry and Market Economics
Investigates competition, pricing, consumer behaviour, productivity, industry structure, and market entry.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Microeconomics, market analysis, industry research, quantitative modelling.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Market Economist, Industry Research Analyst, Economic Consulting Analyst.

rows.text: Regression, model diagnostics, causal inference basics
R or Python; introductory SQL where relevant

blocks.text: Spreadsheets and reporting
Excel or Google Sheets for data cleaning, summary statistics, tables, and charts.
Statistical analysis
R, Python with pandas and statsmodels, or Stata where available. Learn one tool well before adding others.
Economic data sources

Explore the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), World Bank, International Monetary Fund (IMF), and official national accounts and labour statistics.
Academic research
Use Google Scholar, university repositories, and reputable economics journals to review prior studies, research methods, and competing explanations.
Complete at least three projects that demonstrate economic reasoning and data analysis.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Inflation trends in India

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Macroeconomics
Analyse publicly available consumer price inflation data over a selected period. Compare categories or periods and investigate plausible contributing factors using credible sources.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Clean dataset, charts, a short analytical report, and a discussion of limitations. Avoid claiming causation from simple correlations.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Employment and education

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Labour economics
Examine the relationship between education and employment outcomes using an official dataset. Consider age, location, gender, and other relevant variables where the data supports the comparison.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Research question, descriptive statistics, charts, methodology, limitations, and findings.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Economic policy assessment

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Public finance and policy
Select a public programme or economic policy and assess its objectives, costs, intended beneficiaries, and available evidence of outcomes.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Policy brief, stakeholder analysis, evidence review, and clearly qualified recommendations.

For each project, document the question, data source, variables, analytical methods, results, limitations, and conclusions. Keep assumptions explicit and ensure that the data supports the claims made.

How to improve your chances

items.text: Prepare a CV highlighting economics coursework, statistics, data analysis, and research writing.
Create two or three credible research projects using official data.
Learn either R or Python and practise explaining your analytical choices.
Read economic reports and summarise the main findings in your own words.
Apply to research assistant and analyst internships, including university-led research projects.

rows.text: Regression analysis, diagnostics, and causal inference
Excel, R or Python, data visualisation
Financial markets, monetary systems, and financial economics
Policy evaluation, programme assessment, public finance
Technical writing, research briefs, data storytelling

blocks.text: Choose courses from reputable universities, research organisations, or established training providers. A certificate is most useful when paired with an applied project that demonstrates the skill.
For many independent economic research careers, postgraduate study is a significant advantage and may be a formal requirement.
MA / MSc in Economics
A strong route for economic analysis, forecasting, policy research, and research analyst positions. Check mathematics, statistics, and entrance requirements.
Master's in Applied Economics or Econometrics
Suitable for quantitative economic research, modelling, forecasting, and empirical analysis.
Master's in Finance or Financial Economics
Useful for financial-market research, banking, monetary economics, and financial-sector analysis.
Master's in Public Policy or Development Economics
Suitable for policy evaluation, development research, public finance, and socioeconomic analysis.
PhD in Economics
Typically relevant for academic research, advanced theoretical or empirical research, and some senior economist positions.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: An undergraduate Economics & Finance degree can support entry-level research and analyst roles, but it does not automatically qualify someone for every economist position. Check the job description's requirements for mathematics, econometrics, and postgraduate study.

rows.text: Collect data, review literature, prepare charts and summaries
Conduct analysis, maintain datasets, write research sections
Design studies, interpret results, develop forecasts or policy analysis
Lead projects, review methods, guide researchers
Set research priorities, advise decision-makers, lead research teams

blocks.text: Titles and expectations vary by organisation. Academic and advanced policy research pathways may require postgraduate degrees or a doctorate.
Economic researchers may work on:

blocks.label: AI and productivity
blocks.text: Measuring how automation and AI affect employment, wages, and business performance.

blocks.label: Climate economics
blocks.text: Studying climate risk, energy transitions, and environmental policy.

blocks.label: Digital finance
blocks.text: Analysing digital payments, financial inclusion, and consumer credit.

blocks.label: Labour-market change
blocks.text: Investigating skills demand, remote work, and employment transitions.

blocks.label: Development economics
blocks.text: Evaluating poverty reduction, education, health, and social programmes.

blocks.label: Economic forecasting
blocks.text: Using statistical and computational methods to understand potential economic trends.
These are research areas to explore rather than guarantees of job growth.
Use this checklist to track readiness for entry-level economic research roles.
Economic research readiness tracker
I understand fundamental microeconomics and macroeconomics.
I can interpret economic indicators and official datasets.
I can use Excel or Google Sheets for economic analysis.
I understand regression and introductory econometrics.
I can use R or Python for a basic data analysis task.
I can write a research brief with sources and limitations.
I have completed at least two economic research projects.
I can explain findings using charts and concise presentations.
I have tailored my CV and applications for research roles.
Check off items as you build each competency. This is a preparation guide, not a hiring guarantee.
By graduation, a strong candidate should be able to:

items.text: Explain economic events using appropriate economic concepts.
Collect, clean, analyse, and interpret economic data.
Apply statistics and introductory econometric methods responsibly.
Review existing research and identify meaningful research questions.
Communicate findings through clear reports, charts, and presentations.
Demonstrate research ability through projects, internships, or assistantships.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Build a strong foundation in economics, statistics, and Excel, then learn R or Python and complete a research project using official Indian economic data. For more advanced economist roles, plan for postgraduate economics training and deeper econometric skills.
